question: Are coherent accurate maps present among individual rollouts, and does marginal voting hide alternative contact-map patterns?
samples: 200 independent resampled prompts per protein, fixed as pools A and B of 100
primary_comparison: Complete-map F1 for mean, oracle-best and blind-selected individual rollouts versus top-R pooled-vote maps; full-map precision, recall and cardinality accompany F1
secondary_comparison: Emission-order fixed-R precision, with unfilled slots scoring zero; not a substitute for unordered-map F1
oracle: Ground-truth-selected best F1 among 100 or 200 samples; diagnostic upper bound only
blind_selectors: highest mean Jaccard to the opposite independent pool
cluster_probe: Average-linkage clustering of pool A on whole-map Jaccard distance, k=2 and k=4; assign B to A's medoids. Evaluate pooled B votes within clusters of at least 10 B members, report both A-largest-cluster selection and truth-oracle best cluster. Repeat with pools reversed. Clustering never uses truth.
summary: Unweighted mean over proteins, paired differences with 10000 protein bootstrap resamples, seed 345. Report valid denominators and all failures.
validation: Verify all model source sizes and ETags; smoke before production; all 19400 maps must terminate and pass bounds/duplicate/sample-identity checks. Compare each fresh 100-sample pool's mean canonical R-precision to the saved epoch-2 evaluation; investigate discrepancies exceeding 0.005.
causal_limits: Contact-map coherence and 3D geometric feasibility are distinct. No individual rollout is claimed to be a valid structure without a structural check. Selection with truth is never presented as a deployable improvement. No new eval-test read.
